title: How to uninstall cursor in Cursor on Mac: a complete guide for users
metaTitle: How to uninstall Cursor on Mac: easy removal steps
description: Learn how to uninstall Cursor on Mac effectively. Follow our step by step guide to remove the Cursor IDE and clear your application data permanently.
intro: To uninstall Cursor on Mac, quit the application and move it from your Applications folder to the Trash. For a complete removal of all configuration files and cached data, you must also delete the support directories in your Library folder.
tldr: Drag the Cursor app to the Trash.
Remove ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor for a clean slate.
Use Activity Monitor if the app refuses to close.

blocks.text: Why perform a clean uninstall of Cursor on Mac

You might need to remove the application for several reasons. Perhaps you are troubleshooting a persistent bug that a standard update failed to resolve. Maybe you are moving to a different machine and want to ensure a fresh start. Or perhaps you simply need to reclaim space on your disk. Whatever the case, knowing how to uninstall Cursor on Mac correctly ensures no leftover files interfere with your system or future installations.

Cursor stores your extensions, themes, and local editor state outside the main application package. This design choice helps when you update the app, as your settings persist. However, this also means that dragging the icon to the Trash does not remove everything. If you want a truly clean state, you must manually clear the secondary data folders.
Standard removal of the Cursor application

The first phase of the process is simple and follows the standard macOS procedure for any third party application. Before you start, ensure you have saved any active code files or snippets you need to keep.

items: Open the Cursor application if it is not already running.
Press ⌘Q to quit the application completely.
Open Finder and navigate to your Applications folder.
Drag the icon to the Trash in your Dock.
Right click the Trash icon and select Empty Trash to finalize the removal.

blocks.text: If the system reports that the application is in use, it means a background process is still active. You should check your menu bar for any lingering icons. If that does not work, use Activity Monitor to find and kill the process.
Using Activity Monitor to force quit Cursor
Sometimes a process hangs and prevents you from moving the app to the trash. Activity Monitor is the tool for this. Press ⌘Space to open Spotlight, type Activity Monitor, and press Enter.

items: In the search bar at the top right, type Cursor.
Select any processes related to the app.
Click the X button at the top of the window.
Select Force Quit to stop the process immediately.

blocks.text: How to perform a clean uninstall of Cursor on Mac

If you are uninstalling because of a corrupt configuration or a recurring error, you need to go deeper. The application keeps its settings in your user library. Deleting these files is the only way to reset the app entirely.
Deleting these folders will remove all your extensions, keybindings, and custom settings. Export your profile or back up your settings if you want to keep them for a future installation.

These commands target the core configuration directory and the global preferences file. Once these are gone, the application will treat the next launch as a brand new installation.

Users occasionally run into a warning stating that the app is damaged. This is usually a system level issue with how macOS handles app signatures or quarantined files. If you see this, do not panic. Simply move the app to the Trash, empty the Trash, and download a fresh copy from the official website.

Another issue involves disk space. If you find your storage is still full after removing the app, you may have accumulated large cache files. You can clear these from within the app before you uninstall it. Open the Command Palette with ⌘⇧P and look for commands related to clearing chat history or garbage collection.
Cursor web app versus desktop app

It is important to distinguish between the desktop IDE and the browser based interface. The web app at cursor.com/agents does not require any local installation. You cannot uninstall it because it is not on your disk. If you want to stop using it, simply sign out of your account or close the browser tab. This is a common point of confusion for new users.

faq.question: Will I lose my code if I uninstall Cursor?
faq.answer: No. Your source code files are stored in your project directories, not inside the application folder. Uninstalling Cursor only removes the editor software and its internal settings.

faq.question: How do I reinstall Cursor after uninstalling?
faq.answer: Visit the official cursor.com website, download the latest DMG file, and drag the app back to your Applications folder. It will detect your system architecture automatically.

faq.question: Does uninstalling Cursor remove my extensions?
faq.answer: A standard move to Trash might leave extension folders behind in your Library. To remove extensions completely, follow the clean uninstall steps provided in this guide.

steps.name: Quit the application
steps.text: Ensure the Cursor app is completely closed. Use the shortcut ⌘Q or select Quit from the top menu bar.

steps.name: Move to Trash
steps.text: Open your Applications folder in Finder, find the Cursor app, and drag it to the Trash.

steps.name: Clear support files
steps.text: Open Terminal and run the command rm -rf ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor to remove all remaining configuration data.
steps.tip: Be careful with the rm command as it deletes files permanently.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says it is in use and cannot be moved to Trash.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Activity Monitor, search for Cursor, and force quit all related processes.

troubleshooting.problem: Settings persist after a fresh reinstall.
troubleshooting.fix: You did not delete the ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor directory. Perform the clean uninstall steps.
